chunks: As for what Ibn ʿUqdah narrated from Faḍl ibn Yūsuf, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUkkāshah, from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUmārah Abī ʿUmārah al-Ḥārithī, he said:
I asked Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام: Should I wipe my head with the moisture of my hand? He said: “Take fresh water for your head.”

The interpretation here as well is what we have already mentioned regarding taqiyyah, because its narrators are narrators of the ʿĀmmah and the Zaydiyyah. As for his statement, may Allah the Exalted support him, that he wipes his head with the measure of three joined fingers from the forelock to the edge of the hair of his head once, then its proof is as follows.

key_terms.أَمْسَحُ: I wipe; here, the act of masḥ over the head in wudu (ablution).
key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: Taqiyyah; dissimulation or precaution in circumstances requiring concealment.
key_terms.الزَّيْدِيَّةِ: The Zaydiyyah; a distinct Shia group mentioned regarding the narrators.
key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: The general Sunni community; used here for non-Imami transmitters.
key_terms.بِبَلَلِ: With the moisture; referring to the remaining wetness on the hand.
key_terms.قُصَاصِ: The hairline or edge of the hair; the endpoint mentioned for the wipe.
key_terms.مَاءً جَدِيداً: Fresh water; newly taken water for wiping.
key_terms.نَاصِيَتِهِ: His forelock; the front part of the head from which wiping begins.

ai.seo_question: Does this hadith indicate using fresh water to wipe the head in wudu (ablution), and how is it understood in Shia scholarship?
ai.summary: This passage concerns the ruling of wiping the head in wudu (ablution) and cites a report from Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام about using fresh water. It then explains, within the Shia hadith framework, that the report is interpreted in light of taqiyyah because its transmitters are associated with the ʿĀmmah and the Zaydiyyah, while affirming the specific manner of wiping the head once.
